status: Diagnostic evidence; not an adopted energy or uncertainty distribution.

baltayan_nedelec1979.inspection: User-provided publisher PDF, six PDF pages including cover. Complete article printed pp 2399-2403 read; printed p 2399 abstract and p 2401 equations/figure/table visually checked.
baltayan_nedelec1979.quantity: De, measured from the potential minimum
baltayan_nedelec1979.uncertainty_definition: Section IV identifies high-J lifetime precision as the largest uncertainty and high-J level energies (~50 cm^-1) as another contribution. Fig. 4 error bars exclude level-energy uncertainty. The reported +/-0.01 eV has no stated confidence level or probabilistic definition; it must not be treated as a calibrated 1-sigma error.

local_pdf.inspection: User-provided publisher PDF, six PDF pages including cover. Complete article printed pp 2399-2403 read; printed p 2399 abstract and p 2401 equations/figure/table visually checked.
local_pdf.archive_policy: The user-provided full article and extracted full text remain local. The repository retains bibliographic metadata, hash, independently written review notes and selected factual quantities only.

printed_locations: p 2401: Section IV, Fig. 4, Table III and Section V opening

publisher_metadata_discrepancy.resolution: Use the consistent printed abstract and body value 3.16 eV. The previously inspected publisher/Crossref metadata value 3.17 eV is retained only to document the discrepancy; it is not a second measurement.

atomic_asymptote.dissociation_products: Al(3s2 3p 2P) + H(1s 2S), the atomic ground terms
atomic_asymptote.basis: Section IV explicitly lowers the X-state dissociation limit by 100 cm^-1 relative to A for Al(2P) fine structure. Section V identifies the atomic ground terms.
atomic_asymptote.interpretation: The lower X asymptote is consistent with Al(2P1/2)+H(2S1/2); the article does not print resolved J labels. Its De(X) already includes the stated fine-structure offset. Do not subtract a term-center correction again.

baltayan_nedelec1979.method: Sections II-IV combine pulsed-laser radiative lifetimes, emission intensity deficits extrapolated to zero Ar pressure and diffuse-line widths with a semiclassical tunnelling model. The A-state potential uses RKR spectroscopy between v=0 and v=1, Morse continuation on the inner side and a reconstructed outer barrier; the slow outer tail near r>=5 angstrom yields the dissociation limit. This is a spectroscopic potential inference, not a direct dissociation-threshold measurement.

qin2021_independent_theory.limitation: No thermochemical uncertainty is assigned. The first dissociation limit is labelled Al(2P)+H(2S), without a resolved Al J label.

zero_point_diagnostic.constants_source: Experimental row of Qin et al. 2021 Table 1, attributed to Szajna et al. 2011; not a new fit here.
zero_point_diagnostic.formula: G(0) approximately omega_e/2 - omega_ex_e/4; higher Dunham terms omitted.
zero_point_diagnostic.limitation: This two-term spectroscopic zero-point estimate yields D0 about 3.0566 eV, not a newly fitted threshold or complete uncertainty interval. Higher Dunham terms and uncertainty propagation remain unassessed.

al_atomic_fine_structure_diagnostic.inspection: NIST persistent-line level table inspected on 2026-11-02.
al_atomic_fine_structure_diagnostic.interpretation: The term-center scale is retained as a convention diagnostic only. The full 1979 paper explicitly places the X limit below A for fine structure, so no additional 0.0093 eV subtraction is applied. Updating its approximate 100 cm^-1 split to the modern 112.061 cm^-1 would require reconstructing the original potential reference and is not done here.

barklem_collet2016_table1.record_source: Frozen major_molecule_reference.json; column meanings checked against original paper Table 1 and Section 2.1.1.
barklem_collet2016_table1.limitation: The specific original sources behind the Luo AlH entry have not been inspected. Its similarity to JANAF is not proof of common ancestry.

assessment: The printed primary De=3.16 eV, less an approximately 0.1034 eV zero-point energy, gives diagnostic D0=3.0566 eV. This is about 0.0064 eV above NASA-derived 3.0502 eV and 0.1148 eV above JANAF-derived 2.9418 eV. The original explicitly incorporates the X/A fine-structure offset; no extra term-center shift is applied. The full text strengthens the preference for a NASA-like energy and resolves the 3.17/3.16 metadata discrepancy, but does not certify the exact NASA value, a statistical uncertainty distribution, or high-temperature thermal functions. Do not adopt 3.16 eV directly as D0.
